assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a clear chain from basic hormone biology to a treatment class that has changed diabetes and obesity care, with large effects on weight, glycaemia and cardiovascular outcomes. The discovery is original, well defined and of very high lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic role of GLP-1 in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2, translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) are the most defensible three. Knudsen is a major drug-development figure, but the scientific discovery credit is better held by the three; I am relying on recollection of the historical record and have not verified priority details.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent approved drugs, large randomized outcome trials and broad clinical uptake over more than a decade. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority and credit between Mojsov, Habener and others is contested, and the longlist does not credit every contributor.
Whether the committee would prefer to include a drug-development contributor over a discovery contributor.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identification and the framing of nutrient-responsive control of cell growth is a foundational concept in cell physiology with relevance to cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. The discovery is original and conceptually clear, and it organizes a large field.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and carried the core conceptual claim; Schreiber's chemical-biology work on rapamycin target proteins (FKBP12 and mTOR) was decisive for the mechanism. Sabatini contributed mammalian pathway elucidation (mTORC1 nutrient sensing), but I leave him out of the proposal given the unsettled scientific-conduct questions I recall around him, which I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation, extensive mechanistic work, and clinical use of rapalogs; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and the rapamycin discoverers outside the list, such as Heitman, Hall and Sabatini's mammalian work, is unresolved.
Whether the prize should centre on yeast TOR or on the mammalian mTOR pathway.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T-cell therapy has turned refractory haematological malignancies into treatable disease and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept and the clinical proof are both strong, and the impact on oncology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early chimeric receptor and costimulatory design, June led the translation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulatory domains into the first sustained clinical remissions, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified T cells in patients. Other contributors, for example Eshhar and Kuwana, are not on this credited list; the three are the most defensible within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature for haematological cancers, with several approved products and long-term remissions; durability, toxicity and limited solid-tumour success keep some caution, though recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Foundational credit for the chimeric receptor concept is divided and partly outside the credited names.
Long-term outcomes and secondary malignancy signals are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and cell biology a general method for causal, cell-type-specific control with light, and it is used across physiology. It is an invention-style discovery of broad and durable influence.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels, and Deisseroth with Boyden turned them into a neuronal toolkit. The field has too many credible contributors (Bamberg, Miesenböck, Boyden) for three to be clean, which is a real fairness problem; Boyden is a very close alternative to Deisseroth.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent use, with applications emerging in vision restoration, though therapeutic translation is early.
uncertainties: Attribution is the central problem and any three-person set omits major contributors.
Therapeutic validation is limited relative to the tool's research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined how the endoplasmic reticulum signals to the nucleus to adjust folding capacity, with implications for secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is a clear, original and well-understood cellular mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily worked out the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) signalling pathway and are the natural pair; Walter's work on IRE1 and the integrated stress response adds depth. The credit for this core pathway is relatively clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation, and the field has generated drug candidates. Recognition is well timed, though it has long been a recurring candidate.
uncertainties: Direct clinical translation is still developing.
Possible inclusion of other UPR pioneers such as Ron or Kaufman is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, a direct and large benefit to public health. The discovery is original, with strong population-level evidence of cancer prevention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 virus-like particles, and Frazer (with Zhou) developed the VLP expression and the vaccine concept. Credit for the L1 VLP priority is shared with others, for example Zhou and Kirnbauer, which I recall but cannot verify; the three listed names are a plausible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: licensed vaccines, national programmes, and falling rates of HPV infection, cervical precancer and now cancer.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among the several groups that made VLPs, and the Zhou contribution since Zhou died early.
A prior Nobel for HPV and cervical cancer (zur Hausen, 2008) may lower the committee's appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term culture of adult-stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general experimental platform for tissue biology, disease modelling, drug testing and personalized medicine, grounded in the discovery of Lgr5 stem cells. It is original and the impact is broad.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual driver and Sato the lead on the key demonstration of the crypt-villus organoid culture. The two-name configuration is clean and supported by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in research use, but clinical translation is still early and the relationship with other organoid approaches (pluripotent-stem-cell derived) is a nuance.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a method more than a discovery, and the extent of clinical benefit so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition by imatinib is the proof of principle for molecularly targeted cancer therapy, transforming chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease to a chronic condition. The impact is exceptional and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical development and the demonstration of selective efficacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The Lasker award recognized Druker, Lydon and Sawyers, but Rowley and Nowell and Hungerford's earlier cytogenetic work is also a part of the story, and the committee has already honoured parts of the BCR-ABL context in other ways.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with twenty-five years of survival data, though recognition has not yet come for a discovery of this size.
uncertainties: The classical Nobel emphasis on discovery rather than drug development.
Contribution of Ciba-Geigy chemists such as Zimmermann and Matter beyond the credited names.
